extracted.intended_audience: bacteriologists / sanitary laboratory technicians performing environmental microbiology assays
extracted.subtask_description: Standard laboratory protocols and evaluative criteria for quantitative and qualitative bacteriological examination of oysters, sewage, air, soil, for testing filter candles, and for standardised disinfectant assays (including phenol-coefficient determination). Covers sampling, dilution, plating, incubation, enumeration, and identification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial dilution procedure (capsules I–IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange four sterile capsules in a row and number I, II, III, IV; pipette 9 c.c. sterile distilled water (or bouillon) into capsule I and 9.9 c.c. into the remaining capsules; add 1 c.c. of sample to capsule I, mix, transfer 0.1 c.c. from I to II, 0.1 c.c. from II to III, and 0.1 c.c. from III to IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit dilution factors for oysters, sewage, and soil examples (e.g., 1 c.c. of dilution I contains 0.1 c.c. original sewage, etc.). Label carefully and use these dilutions when inoculating media for enumeration and qualitative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plating volumes and incubation for quantitative enumeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour sets of gelatine plates from each dilution containing specified volumes (examples: three plates per set containing 0.2, 0.3, and 0.5 c.c.; or two plates containing 0.1 and 0.4 c.c.). Incubate at appropriate temperatures (commonly 20°C for gelatine media) for three, four, or five days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate colonies on plates which have not liquefied (often from the highest dilutions) and calculate numbers per unit volume of the original sample. For air results express organisms per cubic metre by multiplying appropriate factors (e.g., multiply by 100 because 50 c.c. broth represents 10 litres of air).

rubrics_metrics.name: Air sampling apparatus and aspiration rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an aspirator bottle (10 litres) fitted with delivery tube and Erlenmeyer flask (50 c.c. sterile water) with fitted funnel; regulate flow so the delivery tube yields 1 c.c. of water every second, thereby aspirating 10 litres of air through the water per run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pack the receiving flask in ice, sterilise fittings by boiling, connect assembly, run until aspirator empties (≈just under three hours), then pour plated aliquots of the infected water for enumeration and identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air qualitative plating and incubation regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: For qualitative air exam pour plates of wort agar and nutrient agar and incubate at 37°C; pour wort gelatine plates incubated at 20°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick individual colonies from these plates, subculture on various media, and identify organisms to species using standard cultural and microscopic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil sample collection protocols (surface and deep samples)
rubrics_metrics.description: For surface samples use a sterilised iron scoop (shoe-horn shaped with sharp spine) wrapped/sterilised and protected until use; for deep samples use a borer (e.g., Fraenkel's earth borer) capable of sampling at specified depths and designed to protect and retain the sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sterilise implements (hot-air oven), protect with oiled paper/gutta-percha, brush away debris before sampling. For deep sampling use the borer's flanged sleeve mechanism to receive and retain the sample and sterilise by ether burning or oven as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil quantitative examination categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete quantitative examination includes: (1) enumeration of aerobic organisms; (2) enumeration of spores of aerobes; (3) enumeration of anaerobic organisms (including facultative anaerobes); (4) enumeration of spores of anaerobes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine results (e.g., spore : vegetative ratio) and correct colony counts by wet-to-dry soil weight ratio to report organisms per gramme of soil, yeasts and moulds per gramme, and organisms 'growing at 37°C' per gramme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of 'soil water' and dilution equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Triturate 10 grammes of earth in 100 c.c. sterile bouillon; after settling, 1 c.c. of supernatant 'soil water' contains washings from 0.1 gramme of soil. Further dilutions using the capsule dilution series yield defined soil-equivalents (e.g., 1 c.c. from capsule I = .01 gm earth, from II = .0001 gm, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform weighing, trituration, and some steps under a hood to avoid contamination. Use these equivalents to calculate organisms per gramme after plating and counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plating media and incubation for aerobes/anaerobes and spores
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour gelatine, wort gelatine, and agar plates from specified capsules and incubate at 20°C or 37°C as indicated; to enumerate spores, heat soil water at 80°C for ten minutes then pour plates containing 0.1–1 c.c. and incubate one set aerobically and another anaerobically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anaerobes incubate plates in Bulloch's anaerobic apparatus. Delay enumeration as long as possible for spore counts. Calculate spore counts and ratios between spores and total forms for both aerobic and anaerobic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and approach for qualitative soil examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative soil exam is aimed at detecting: Coli-typhoid group members, streptococci, Bacillus anthracis, Bacillus tetani, Bacillus oedematis maligni, nitrous and nitric organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter the soil water, suspend the bacterial residue in bouillon (so that 1 c.c. suspension approximates to the soil water from ~1 gramme), then proceed with isolation techniques as described elsewhere (similar to water methods) and organism-specific steps follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of nitrous and nitric organisms (Winogradsky methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Winogradsky's solutions I and II: inoculate ten tubes numbered 1–10 with specified volumes from soil water and dilution capsules (combinations of 1.0 and 0.1 c.c. from soil water and capsules I–IV), label and incubate at 30°C; examine after 24 and 48 hours and subculture tubes showing growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From positive subcultures make further subcultivations, prepare surface smears on Winogradsky's silicate jelly, pick colonies and subculture to obtain isolates for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical testing of porcelain filter candles for flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach the actual filter candle to a powerful pump (e.g., foot bicycle pump with manometer), immerse candle in water and raise internal pressure gradually to two atmospheres; inspect for streams of air bubbles to reveal cracks or flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies physical defects that would allow bacterial passage irrespective of structural integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterility/permeability test for filters using test bacteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Emulsify surface growth of Bacillus mycoides in sterile saline, dilute to 1000 c.c., filter through the sterilised candle, pour six agar plates each containing 1 c.c. of filtrate and incubate at 37°C up to seven days; if filtrate is sterile repeat using smaller organisms (B. prodigiosus, then a very small coccus such as Micrococcus melitensis with 14 days incubation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filtrate yields growth, identify organism to confirm whether it is the test bacterium (to rule out contamination) before rejecting the filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and preparation of test germ for disinfectant assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Select B. coli as the test germ because of its relative nonpathogenicity, ease of isolation and identification, stability of characters, and evenness of resistance; prepare a stock agar culture, smear culture anaerobically at 37°C for 24 hours, emulsify surface growth in 10 c.c. sterile water, homogenise with glass beads and centrifuge to obtain a supernatant emulsion for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a stock culture plated at least twice to ensure purity; the described preparation yields a homogeneous emulsion suitable for accurate inoculation in disinfectant tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germicide preparation and standard control (phenol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine inhibition coefficient of germicide-x, then prepare various solutions by volumetric methods beginning somewhat stronger than the inhibition coefficient; prepare control phenol solutions (examples: 1.1%, 1.0%, 0.9%, 0.75%, 0.7%, 0.65%) freshly each day by weighing carbolic acid and dissolving to volume in standardised flasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare solutions in bulk (not less than 5 c.c. of disinfectant for any given percentage solution). Use phenol as the standard germicide for comparison because of its uniform composition and established use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and procedural conditions for disinfectant assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain controlled environment: close windows/doors, disinfect work bench, minimise movement; contact temperature 15–18°C (prefer 18°C); proportional bulk of test germ to germicide 50:1 (e.g., 5 c.c. germicide + 0.1 c.c. emulsion); remove 0.1 c.c. sample at each contact time; subculture into bile salt broth; incubate subcultures at 37°C and observe up to seven days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust medium volume in subculture tubes according to inhibition coefficient (10 c.c. is routine but may need 12–15 c.c.); bile salt broth chosen because it dilutes carried-over germicide and is selective for intestinal bacteria; use signs (+) for growth and (-) for no growth and identify organisms via characteristic reactions, plating, carbohydrate media and agglutination where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary tests: inhibition coefficient and trial trip
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Determine inhibition coefficient: the lowest percentage of germicide-x that inhibits growth and the highest percentage that fails to inhibit. (b) Trial trip: test a series of five solutions of germicide-x at contact times 2½, 5, 25 and 30 minutes to identify concentrations that bracket lethal values at 2½ and 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the trial trip results to select concentrations for the final comparative test. The manual gives an explicit step-by-step inoculation timetable and handling precautions (use of pipette+washer assembly, timed inoculations, and rapid transfer to subculture tubes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final test and determination of phenol coefficient (paired comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct paired tests of germicide-x and standard phenol using concentrations preselected from the trial trip that include lethal dilutions at 2½ and 30 minutes; arrange test tubes of germicide-x and two sets of labelled bile salt broth tubes for timed subcultures to record times to inactivation for both germicide-x and phenol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the relative lethal dilutions/timepoints of germicide-x and phenol to compute a phenol coefficient according to standard methods (procedure continued in following steps beyond this chunk).
